title: The Shifting Mystery of Beika City
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure, Takagi, Chiba) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. The old cases/ file's murderer_id (Kanemitsu Toyoko) was actually CORRECT, unlike some other rebuilt episodes, but the old file was extremely thin: it used a single generic 'knows' edge for every suspect->victim link, had no framing mechanics, no locked-room/staged-suicide circumstance detail, and omitted several plot-load-bearing named characters entirely (Chino Yosuke, the framed academic; Eiko Hayama, the housekeeper whose timing testimony narrows the culprit's window; Koyuki Gamo, the waitress-witness; Ichimura Zetto, the magazine editor who confirms the motive chain). The old file's single clue (books removed from the café) is now decomposed into two genuinely comparative clue nodes: the two magazines sharing the pen name Dorosue Yamiyo, and the housekeeper's before/after account of the lighter under the sofa. case_type: murder. The real motive (literary revenge against critic Chino Yosuke) only surfaces via a secondary pen-name investigation thread the old file's 'mystery books' object gestured at but never explained.

clues.desc: Both a Labyrinths magazine and a Mystery World magazine displayed at Kanemitsu's café feature the same little-known author name, Dorosue Yamiyo -- an unusual pattern that identifies Kanemitsu as that pen name's owner.

The housekeeper confirms Chino's lighter was not under the sofa when she left Bando's house at dusk but was there when police searched -- proving it was planted by whoever visited that evening, not by Chino during his earlier afternoon visit.
